semin-durr:50-50.t: His saying: {فَبِأَيِّ حَدِيثٍ}: it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to His saying «يُؤمنون», i.e. if they do not believe in this Qur'an, then in what thing will they believe? The majority read it in the third person (al-ghayba). Ibn ʿĀmir, in one transmission, and Yaʿqūb read it in the second person (al-khiṭāb), by way of iltifāt (shift of address) or of transition.

semin-durr:1-1.t:
His saying: {عُرْفاً}: there are three aspects to it. The first: it is a mafʿūl li-ajlihi (object of purpose), i.e. for the sake of al-ʿurf, which is the opposite of al-nukr (the reprehensible). What is meant by «المُرْسَلات» is either the angels, or the prophets, or the winds, i.e. by the angels sent forth, or the prophets sent forth, or the winds sent forth. And al-ʿurf is kindness (al-maʿrūf) and beneficence. The poet said:
4454 - مَنْ يَفْعَلِ الخيرَ لا يَعْدَمْ جَوازِيَهُ ... لا يَذْهَبُ العُرْفُ بينَ اللَّهِ والناسِ
(Whoever does good will not lack its rewards; kindness is not lost between Allah and people.)
It may be said: how did He pluralise the attribute of a rational masculine with alif and tāʾ, when it should properly be pluralised with wāw and nūn? You say «الأنبياءُ المُرْسَلونَ», and you do not say «المُرْسَلات». The answer is that «المُرْسَلات» is the plural of mursala, and mursala is an attribute of a group of prophets; so «المُرْسَلات» is the plural of «مُرْسَلة» occurring as an attribute of a group, not the plural of the singular «مُرْسَل». The second: that it is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) in the sense of "successive", from their saying: they came like the mane (ʿurf) of a horse, and they are against so-and-so like the mane of a hyena, when they gang up against him. The third: that it is accusative by removal of the preposition, i.e. those sent with al-ʿurf.
There is weakness in this [last aspect]. The discussion of al-ʿurf preceded in al-Aʿrāf. The generality [of readers] have a sukūn on its rāʾ, and ʿĪsā [read it] with ḍamma; that is by making heavy what is light, as in «بَكُر» for bakr. It is possible that it is the original, with the well-known [reading] lightened from it, and it is possible that they are two independent patterns.

semin-durr:2-2.t: His saying: {عَصْفاً}: a maṣdar (verbal noun) emphasising the active participle. What is meant by «العاصفات» is the winds or the angels, likened to the winds in the swiftness of their course in the command of Allah the Exalted. Likewise «نَشْراً» and «فَرْقاً» are also accusative as maṣdars.

semin-durr:5-5.t: His saying: {ذِكْراً}: a mafʿūl bihi (direct object), governed by «المُلْقِيات». The generality [of readers] read «فالمُلْقِياتِ» with a sukūn on the lām and a light qāf, an active participle. Ibn ʿAbbās [read it] with fatḥa on the lām and a doubled qāf, from al-talqiya, which is conveying speech to the one addressed. al-Mahdawī also narrated from him fatḥa on the qāf, a passive participle, i.e. cast from the side of Allah the Exalted.

semin-durr:6-6.t:
His saying: {عُذْراً أَوْ نُذْراً}: there are several aspects to them. The first: they are two badals (substitutes) from «ذِكْراً». The second: they are accusative by it as objects, and making a maṣdar with tanwīn govern is permissible; among it is {أَوْ إِطْعَامٌ فِي يَوْمٍ ذِي مَسْغَبَةٍ يَتِيماً} [al-Balad: 14-15]. The third: they are mafʿūl li-ajlihi (objects of purpose), and what governs them is either «المُلْقِيات» or «ذِكْراً», because each of them is fit to be caused by one of the two. In that case two aspects are permissible in «عُذْراً» and «نُذْراً»: the first, that they are maṣdars with a quiescent middle radical, like al-shukr and al-kufr; the second, that they are the plurals of ʿadhīr and nadhīr, by which the maṣdar is meant, in the sense of excusing (iʿdhār) and warning (indhār), like al-nakīr in the sense of al-inkār. The fourth: they are accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «المُلْقِيات» or from the pronoun in it. In that case they may be maṣdars occurring in the place of a ḥāl by the well-known interpretation in such cases; or plurals of ʿadhīr and nadhīr by which the maṣdar is meant, or by which the active participle is meant in the sense of al-muʿdhir and al-mundhir, i.e. excusing or warning.
The generality [of readers] read with a sukūn on the dhāl of «عُذْراً» and «نُذْراً». Zayd ibn Thābit, Ibn Khārija and Ṭalḥa read with ḍamma on it; and the two Ḥaramīs [Nāfiʿ and Ibn Kathīr], Ibn ʿĀmir and Abū Bakr with sukūn in «عُذْراً» and ḍamma in «نُذُراً». The sukūn and ḍamma are as preceded, in that each of them may be the origin of the other, or they may be two independent origins; and each of the heavy and the light may be a maṣdar, or a plural whose middle radical was made quiescent for lightness. Ibrāhīm al-Taymī read «عُذْراً ونُذْراً» with the conjunctive wāw in place of «أو», which indicates that «أو» is in the sense of the wāw.

semin-durr:7-7.t: His saying: {إِنَّ مَا تُوعَدُونَ}: this is the apodosis of the oath in His saying «والمُرْسَلاتِ», and what follows it is conjoined to it, not an independent oath, for what preceded at the beginning of this work, and because the fāʾ occurs as a conjunction, since it is not [a particle] of oath. «ما» is a relative noun in the sense of «الذي», the noun of «إنَّ», and «تُوْعَدون» is its ṣila (relative clause), the returning pronoun being omitted, i.e. that which you are promised. And «لَواقعٌ» is its khabar. «إنَّ» should properly have been written separate from the relative «ما», but they wrote it joined to it.

semin-durr:8-8.t: His saying: {فَإِذَا النجوم طُمِسَتْ}: «النجومُ» is nominative by an implied verb explained by what follows it, according to the Basrans other than al-Akhfash; and as mubtadaʾ (subject) according to the Kufans and al-Akhfash. Regarding the apodosis of «إذا» there are two views. The first: it is omitted, its implied form being: when the stars are obliterated, what you are promised will occur — because of the indication of His saying «إنَّ ما تُوْعَدُوْن لَواقعٌ» — or: the matter will become clear. The second: it is {لأَيِّ يَوْمٍ أُجِّلَتْ}, on the implying of a verb of saying, i.e. it will be said: for what day ...; so the verb [of saying] is in reality the apodosis. It was also said: the apodosis is «ويلٌ يومئذٍ»; Makkī transmitted it, and it is a mistake, because if it were the apodosis the fāʾ would be required for it, since it is a nominal clause.

semin-durr:11-11.t: His saying: {أُقِّتَتْ}: Abū ʿAmr read «وُقِّتَتْ» with the wāw, and the rest «أُقِّتَتْ» with a hamza in place of the wāw. They said: [the wāw] is the original, because it is from al-waqt (time), and the hamza is a substitute for it because it has a permanent ḍamma. Mention of this has preceded at the beginning of this work.

semin-durr:12-12.t: His saying: {لأَيِّ يَوْمٍ}: attached to (mutaʿalliq) «أُجِّلَتْ». This clause is governed by an implied verb of saying, i.e. it will be said. This implied saying may be the apodosis of «إذا», as preceded, or a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the nominative of «أُقِّتَتْ», i.e. it being said concerning them: for what day were they deferred?

semin-durr:13-13.t: His saying: {لِيَوْمِ الفصل}: a badal (substitute) from «لأيِّ يومٍ», with repetition of the governing element. It was also said: rather, it is attached to an implied verb, i.e. they were deferred to the Day of Decision. It was also said: the lām is in the sense of «إلى»; Makkī mentioned both.

semin-durr:15-15.t: His saying: {وَيْلٌ}: a mubtadaʾ (subject); what permits beginning with it [though indefinite] is its being an imprecation. al-Zamakhsharī said: «If you say: how did the indefinite occur as mubtadaʾ in His saying "وَيْلٌ"? I say: in its origin it is an accusative maṣdar standing in place of its verb, but it was diverted to the nominative to indicate the permanence and continuance of the meaning of destruction for those imprecated against; similar to it is {سَلاَمٌ عَلَيْكُمْ} [al-Anʿām: 54]. "وَيْلاً له" in the accusative is permissible, but it was not read so.» I say: what he mentioned is not among the justifications [for an indefinite mubtadaʾ] that the grammarians enumerated; the justification is only what I mentioned to you, its being an imprecation. The benefit of diverting it to the nominative is what he mentioned. And «يومئذٍ» is an adverb (ẓarf) for «الوَيْل». Abū al-Baqāʾ permitted it to be an attribute of «وَيْلٌ», with «للمُكَذِّبين» its khabar (predicate).

semin-durr:16-16.t:
His saying: {أَلَمْ نُهْلِكِ}: the generality [of readers] have ḍamma on the imperfect prefix, from the quadriliteral «أَهْلَكَ». Qatāda [read it] with fatḥa. al-Zamakhsharī said: «From halakahu, in the sense of ahlakahu (he destroyed him). al-ʿAjjāj said:
4455 - ومَهْمَهٍ هالكِ مَنْ تعرَّجا
(And many a desert waste, destroyer of whoever turns aside into it.)»
I say: so «مَنْ» is governed by «هالك», and it is from halaka. However, some people made this a proof for the resembling adjective (al-ṣifa al-mushabbaha) governing a relative noun, and made it from the intransitive, because the condition of the resembling adjective is that it be from an intransitive verb; on this basis there is no proof in it.

semin-durr:17-17.t:
His saying: {ثُمَّ نُتْبِعُهُمُ}: the generality [of readers] have the ʿayn in the nominative, as resumptive, i.e. then We shall make them follow; so Abū al-Baqāʾ rendered it [as "then We, We make them follow"]. He said: «It is not conjoined, because conjunction would require the meaning to be: We destroyed the former ones, then We made the later ones follow them in destruction; and it is not so, because the destruction of the later ones has not yet occurred.» I say: in the resumptive aspect there is no need to posit a mubtadaʾ before the verb; rather, the verb is made conjoined to the whole clause of His saying «ألم نُهْلِك». This resumption is indicated by the reading of ʿAbd Allāh «ثم سَنُتْبِعُهم» with the sīn of futurity.
al-Aʿraj, and al-ʿAbbās from Abū ʿAmr, read it with a sukūn. There are two aspects to it. The first: it is making the nominative quiescent, so it is resumptive like the overtly nominative. The second: it is conjoined to a jussive. Those meant by "the later ones" are then the people of Shuʿayb, Lūṭ and Mūsā, and by "the former ones" the people of Nūḥ, ʿĀd and Thamūd.

semin-durr:18-18.t: His saying: {كَذَلِكَ نَفْعَلُ}: i.e. like that hideous act, We do with everyone who commits crimes.

semin-durr:23-23.t:
His saying: {فَقَدَرْنَا}: Nāfiʿ and al-Kisāʾī read it with doubling (shadda), from al-taqdīr (determining), which agrees with His saying: {مِن نُّطْفَةٍ خَلَقَهُ فَقَدَّرَهُ} [ʿAbasa: 19]. The rest [read it] light, from al-qudra (power); this is indicated by His saying «فنِعْمَ القادِرون». On the first reading the meaning may be: how excellent are We who are able to determine it; and if «القادِرون» is made in the sense of «المُقَدِّرُون», it is a combination of two words whose meaning is one. Among this is His saying, Exalted is He: {فَمَهِّلِ الكافرين أَمْهِلْهُمْ رُوَيْداً} [al-Ṭāriq: 17], and the saying of al-Aʿshā:
4456 - وأَنْكَرَتْني وما كان الذي نَكِرَتْ ... من الحوادِث إلاَّ الشَّيْبَ والصَّلعَا
(She did not recognise me, and what she found strange among the vicissitudes was nothing but grey hair and baldness.)

semin-durr:25-25.t:
His saying: {كِفَاتاً}: al-kifāt is a name for the container in which something is gathered (yukfatu), i.e. collected; Abū ʿUbayda said this. One says: kafatahu yakfituhu, i.e. he gathered it and drew it together. In the ḥadīth: «Gather in (ikfitū) your children.» al-Ṣamṣāma ibn al-Ṭirimmāḥ said:
4457 - وأنتَ اليوم فوقَ الأرضِ حَيّاً ... وأنتَ غداً تَضُمُّك في كِفاتِ
(Today you are alive upon the earth, and tomorrow it will hold you in a container.)
It was also said: al-kifāt is a name for what gathers, like al-ḍimām and al-jimāʿ; one says: this chapter is the jimāʿ (comprehensive gathering) of the chapters. Regarding its accusative there are two aspects. The first: it is the second object of «نَجْعَلْ», because it is [a verb] of transformation (taṣyīr). The second: it is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الأرضَ», with the second object being «أحياءً وأمواتاً», in the sense of: did We not make it living with plants and dead without plants, i.e. part of it so and part of it so. It was also said: kifāt is the plural of kāfit, like ṣiyām and qiyām as plurals of ṣāʾim and qāʾim. It was also said: rather, it is a maṣdar (verbal noun), like al-kitāb and al-ḥisāb.

semin-durr:26-26.t:
His saying: {أَحْيَآءً}: there are several aspects to it. The first: it is accusative by «كِفات»; Makkī said this, and al-Zamakhsharī, who began with it — after having made «كِفاتاً» the name of what gathers, as in their saying al-ḍimām and al-jimāʿ. This prevents «كِفاتاً» from governing «أحياءً» in the accusative, because it is not one of the governing nouns. Likewise if we make it in the sense of the container, according to the view of Abū ʿUbayda, it does not govern either; the grammarians have explicitly stated that nouns of place, time and instrument, even if they are derived and run on the pattern of verbs, do not govern, such as marmā and minjal; and regarding the noun of the maṣdar (ism maṣdar) there is a well-known disagreement. Their accusative by «كِفات» only works according to the view of Abū al-Baqāʾ, for he permitted only that it be the plural of an active participle or a maṣdar, and both are governing nouns.
The second aspect: that it is accusative by an implied verb indicated by «كِفات», i.e. it gathers them living on its back and dead in its belly; al-Zamakhsharī gave this second.
The third: that the two are accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from «الأرضَ» with the omission of a muḍāf, i.e. possessing living and dead.
The fourth: that the two are accusative as a ḥāl from something omitted, i.e. it gathers you living and dead, because it is known that it is a container for humans; al-Zamakhsharī said this, and Makkī inclined to it, except that he rendered it in the third person, i.e. the earth gathers them in these two states.
The fifth: that the two are accusative as the second object of «نَجْعل», with «كِفاتاً» a ḥāl, as its establishment preceded. The indefiniteness of «أحياءً وأمواتاً» is either for magnification, i.e. it gathers living who cannot be estimated and dead who cannot be counted; or for partitiveness, because the living and the dead of humans are not all the living nor all the dead. Likewise the indefiniteness in «ماءً فُراتاً» admits both meanings too: as for magnification, it is clear, because of the greatness of the favour of it upon them; as for partitiveness, it is like His saying, Exalted is He: {وَيُنَزِّلُ مِنَ السمآء مِن جِبَالٍ فِيهَا مِن بَرَدٍ} [al-Nūr: 43], which conveys partitiveness, and the Qurʾān explains itself.
And al-shāmikhāt is the plural of «شامِخ», which is the very lofty; from it is «شَمَخَ بأَنْفِه» (he raised his nose) when he was arrogant; it was made a metonymy for that, like "turning the side" and "turning the cheek", even if none of that actually takes place.

semin-durr:29-29.t: His saying: {انطلقوا}: i.e. that will be said to them. The generality [of readers] read the second «انطَلِقوا» like the first, in the imperative form, for emphasis. Ruways from Yaʿqūb [read] «انطلَقوا» with fatḥa on the lām, a past verb, as a statement, i.e. when they were commanded, they complied with that. This is a place for the fāʾ, so the construction should have been «فانطَلَقوا», as in your saying: I said "Go" and he went; the absence of the fāʾ here is not clear.

semin-durr:31-31.t: His saying: {لاَّ ظَلِيلٍ}: an attribute of «ظلٍّ», and «لا» comes between the attribute and the thing described to convey negation. The first attribute was brought as a noun and the second as a verb, to indicate the negation of the established and settled presence of this attribute for the shade, and the negation of the renewal and occurrence of availing against the flame.

semin-durr:32-32.t:
His saying: {إِنَّهَا}: i.e. Jahannam, because the whole context is about it. The generality [of readers] read «بَشرَرٍ» with fatḥa on the shīn and no alif between the two rāʾs; Warsh thins (yuraqqiqu) the first rāʾ because of the kasra of the one after it. Ibn ʿAbbās and Ibn Miqsam read with kasra on the shīn and an alif between the two rāʾs; and ʿĪsā likewise, except that he gave the shīn fatḥa. The reading of Ibn ʿAbbās may be the plural of sharara, faʿala being pluralised on fiʿāl, as in raqaba and riqāb, raḥaba and riḥāb; or it may be the plural of sharr not meant as the elative of preference (afʿal al-tafḍīl): one says rajulun sharrun and rijālun shirār, rajulun khayrun and rijālun khiyār, and both take the feminine, so one says imraʾatun sharra and imraʾatun khayra. If preference is meant by them, that is impossible for both, and they are subject to rules mentioned in the books of the grammarians. That is: it throws evil ones (shirār) of punishment, or evil ones of creation.
As for the reading of ʿĪsā, it is the plural of sharāra with the alif, and that is the dialect of Tamīm. al-Sharara and al-sharāra are what flies off from the fire scattered (sparks).
His saying: {كالقصر}: the generality [of readers] have fatḥa on the qāf and sukūn on the ṣād, and it is the well-known palace (qaṣr); [the sparks] are likened to it in size and greatness. Ibn ʿAbbās and his two students Ibn Jubayr and Ibn Jabr, and al-Ḥasan, [read] with fatḥa on the qāf and the ṣād; it is the plural of qaṣara with fatḥa, and al-qaṣara is the necks of camels and of palm trees, and the stumps of trees. Ibn Jubayr and al-Ḥasan also read with kasra on the qāf and fatḥa on the ṣād, the plural of «قَصَرة», meaning with fatḥa on the qāf. al-Zamakhsharī said: «Like ḥāja and ḥiwaj», and the Shaykh said: «Like ḥalaqa (a ring) of iron and ḥilaq.» And «كالقَصِرِ» was read with fatḥa on the qāf and kasra on the ṣād, and I have not seen a justification for it. It appears that it is of the type of itbāʿ (vowel harmony): the origin is «كالقَصْرِ» with a quiescent ṣād, then the ṣād was made to follow the vowel of the rāʾ, so it was given kasra. And if they have done that with what is occupied by a vowel, as in katif and kabid, then for them to do it with what is free of a vowel is all the more fitting. It may also be through transfer (naql), in the sense that he paused on the word and transferred the kasra of the rāʾ to the quiescent letter before it, then treated the connected reading like the pause; this is a widespread type among the readers and grammarians. ʿAbd Allāh read it with ḍamma on both. There are two aspects to it. The first: it is the plural of qaṣr, like rahn and ruhun; al-Zamakhsharī said this. The second: it is shortened from quṣūr, as in [the poet's] saying:
4458 - فيها عيايِيْلُ أُسودٍ ونُمُرْ
(In it are prowling lions and leopards.)
He means numūr, but shortened it; and as in his saying «النُّجُم», meaning al-nujūm. al-Zamakhsharī's derivation is preferable, because the place of the second is either poetic necessity or rarity.

semin-durr:33-33.t:
His saying: {جِمَالَةٌ}: the two brothers [Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī] and Ḥafṣ read «جِمالَةٌ», and the rest «جِمالات». Regarding «الجِمالَة» there are two aspects. The first: it is an explicit plural, the tāʾ being for the feminine of the plural; one says jamal, jimāl and jimāla, like dhakar, dhikār and dhikāra, and ḥajar and ḥijāra. The second: it is a collective noun (ism jamʿ), like al-dhikāra and al-ḥijāra; Abū al-Baqāʾ said this, and the first is the view of the grammarians. As for «جِمالات», it may be the plural of this «جِمالة», or the plural of jimāl, so it would be a plural of a plural. It may also be the plural of the singular jamal, as in their saying «رجِالات قريش» — so they said. This is questionable, because they explicitly stated that non-rational primitive (jāmid) nouns are not pluralised with alif and tāʾ unless they have no broken plural; if they have a broken plural, they are not [so] pluralised. They said: for that reason al-Mutanabbī was declared to have erred in his saying:
4459 - إذا كان بعضُ الناسِ سَيْفاً لدولةٍ ... ففي الناسِ بُوْقاتٌ لها وطُبولُ
(If some people are a sword for a dynasty, then among people there are trumpets and drums for it.)
For he pluralised «بُوق» as «بُوقات» although they say «أَبْواق»; likewise «جِمالات» although they say jamal and jimāl. Moreover, some do not permit that at all and consider the likes of ḥammāmāt and sijillāt anomalous, even though they have no broken plural.
Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Ḥasan, Ibn Jubayr, Qatāda and Abū Rajāʾ — with disagreement [in transmission] from them — read it likewise, except that they gave the jīm ḍamma; these are the ropes of ships. It was also said: the cables of bridges, the singular being «جُمْلة», because it comprises strands of ropes. There are two aspects to it. The first: that «جُمالات» be the plural of jumāl, and jumāl the plural of jumla — so the Shaykh said; but establishing that jumāl with ḍamma is the plural of jumla with ḍamma needs transmission. The second: that «جُمالات» be the plural of jumāla; al-Zamakhsharī said this, and it is apparent. Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Sulamī and Abū Ḥaywa read «جُمالة» with ḍamma on the jīm, and this supports what al-Zamakhsharī just said.
His saying: {صُفْرٌ}: an attribute of «جِمالات» or of «جِمالة», because it is either a plural or a collective noun. The generality [of readers] have a sukūn on the fāʾ, plural of ṣafrāʾ, and al-Ḥasan [read] with ḍamma on it, as if it were itbāʿ (vowel harmony). The simile here is of the utmost eloquence. al-Zamakhsharī said: «It was said: "ṣufr" means black tending to yellow. In the poetry of ʿImrān ibn Ḥiṭṭān the Khārijite:
4460 - دَعَتْهُمْ بأعلَى صوتِها ورَمَتْهُمُ ... بمثل الجِمال الصفر نَزَّاعةِ الشَّوى
(It called them with its loudest voice and pelted them with the like of yellow camels, stripping off the scalps.)
And Abū al-ʿAlāʾ al-Maʿarrī said:
4461 - حمراءُ ساطِعَةُ الذوائب في الدُّجَى ... تَرْمي بكل شَرارةٍ كطِرافٍ
(Red, its flames shining in the darkness, it throws every spark like a leather tent.)
So he likened it to al-ṭirāf, which is a tent of leather, in greatness and redness; it seems he intended, in his wickedness, to outdo the simile of the Qurʾān. And in his self-satisfaction at the imagined surpassing that was made attractive to him, he brought at the beginning of his verse the word "حمراءُ" (red), as preparation for it, proclaiming it and alerting the hearers to its place. He was blind — may Allah combine for him the blindness of both abodes — to His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: "كأنه جِمالةٌ صُفْرٌ", which is equivalent to saying "like a red tent". Moreover, in the likening to the qaṣr, which is the fortress, there is likening from two aspects: in respect of greatness and in respect of height in the air; and in the likening to the jimālāt, which are the cables, there is likening from three aspects: length, greatness and yellowness» — end of quote. A little before that he had said: «They are likened to palaces, then to camels, to make the simile clear; do you not see that they liken camels to al-afdān?» I say: al-afdān are palaces, and it is as though he is alluding to the saying of ʿAntara:
4462 - فوقَفْتُ فيها ناقتي وكأنَّها ... فَدَنٌ لأَقْضِيَ حاجةَ المُتَلَوِّمِ
(So I halted my she-camel there, and she was like a palace, that I might fulfil the need of one who lingers.)

semin-durr:35-35.t: His saying: {هذا يَوْمُ لاَ يَنطِقُونَ}: the generality [of readers] have «يومُ» in the nominative as the khabar (predicate) of «هذا». Zayd ibn ʿAlī, al-Aʿraj, al-Aʿmash, Abū Ḥaywa, and ʿĀṣim in some of his chains, [read it] with fatḥa. There are two aspects to it. The first: the fatḥa is a fatḥa of indeclinability (bināʾ), and it is the khabar of «هذا», as has preceded. The second: it is accusative as an adverb (ẓarf), occurring as the khabar of «هذا», on the basis that [«هذا»] points to the threat that preceded, as if it were said: this punishment mentioned will be on a day on which they do not speak. Something similar to this preceded at the end of al-Māʾida in His saying: {هذا يَوْمُ يَنفَعُ}, except that the accusative there is mutawātir.

semin-durr:36-36.t: His saying: {وَلاَ يُؤْذَنُ}: the generality [of readers] have it with the agent unnamed (passive). al-Ahwāzī related from Zayd ibn ʿAlī «ولا يَأْذَنُ», naming the agent, who is Allah the Exalted. Regarding the nominative of «فيعتذرون» there are two aspects. The first: it is resumptive, i.e. so they make excuses. Abū al-Baqāʾ said: «The meaning would be that they do not speak with speech that benefits them, or they speak at some stations and do not speak at others.» The second: it is conjoined to «يُؤْذن», so it is negated; «had it been put in the accusative, it would have been caused by it.» Ibn ʿAṭiyya said: «It was not put in the accusative as the answer to the negation because of the resemblance of the verse-endings; both aspects are permissible» — end of quote. So he made the impossibility of the accusative merely a matter of verbal correspondence, and the apparent sense of this, together with his saying «both aspects are permissible», is that they have one meaning; but it is not so — rather, the nominative has a meaning other than the meaning of the accusative. al-Aʿlam held a view like this, that the verb may be put in the nominative while its meaning is that of the accusative, and Ibn ʿUṣfūr refuted him.

semin-durr:41-41.t: His saying: {فِي ظِلاَلٍ}: this is the reading of the generality, the plural of ẓill. al-Aʿmash [read] «ظُلَلٍ», the plural of ẓulla. Its like preceded in Yā Sīn, except that both [readings] there are mutawātir.

semin-durr:43-43.t:
His saying: {كُلُواْ}: governed by a verb of saying; that saying is accusative as a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the latent pronoun in the adverbial phrase, i.e. being in shades, it being said to them that. Likewise {كُلُواْ وَتَمَتَّعُواْ قَلِيلاً}: if that is said to them in this world, it is clear; and if it is said in the Hereafter, it is a reminder of their state, i.e. they deserve to have been told such-and-such in their worldly life. Its like:
4463 - إخْوَتي لا تَبْعَدُوا أبداً ... وبَلَى واللَّهِ قد بَعِدُوا
(My brothers, may you never perish! — and yes, by Allah, they have perished.)
That is: they are worthy of having that prayer made for them.
